info.title: HelloHop public API
info.description: HTTP API authenticated with a channel key or an account key. An account key works on every owned number and the account-wide operations documented here. Billing, number create/delete, key management, team, grants and terms acceptance stay in the console. Errors are JSON with a stable `code` and a human-readable `error`. The product name and the origin are filled in when the document is served.

Requires an account key. A channel key cannot access this operation.

get.description: Read whether this channel stores history sent by its paired phone. Stored synced messages are marked source: history_sync in conversation reads.
get.summary: Read whether this channel stores synced history

store_history_sync.description: Whether history the paired phone sends is stored and readable through the conversation read (marked `source: history_sync`). Off by default.

put.summary: Turn storing synced history on or off for this channel
put.description: Off by default. When on, messages the paired phone sends as history are kept in this channel's message log, under the same retention as every other message, and returned by the conversation read with `source: history_sync`. That history arrives when a number is linked (turn this on before linking to receive up to 200 recent messages per chat, from within the message retention period) and when you ask for it with a history request. Turning it off stops storing; what was stored stays until retention removes it. The gateway does not read or use this content; it only stores it for your channel.

store_history_sync.description: Whether history the paired phone sends is stored and readable through the conversation read (marked `source: history_sync`). Off by default.

post.summary: Ask the paired phone for older messages of one chat
post.description: Asks the phone linked to this channel for up to `count` messages of this chat older than the oldest one this channel holds, so a number linked earlier can fill in a conversation without linking again. The phone answers later; the messages then appear in the conversation read with `source: history_sync`. The channel must have `store_history_sync` on (otherwise 409 `history_sync_off`) and must hold at least one message of the chat (otherwise 404 `no_history_anchor`). At most one request per channel every 30 seconds and per chat every 5 minutes (429 `history_request_too_soon`, with Retry-After). Each request is recorded in your API access records. Whether the phone answers, and how much, is up to the phone.

count.description: How many older messages to ask for.

chat_jid.description: The chat the phone was asked about.

before_message_id.description: The answer will be older than this message.

get.description: List up to 100 chats known to the named channel. The response contains a chats array and may include its source.

get.summary: Read a conversation (a person or a group), newest first, one page at a time
get.description: Reads this channel's own message log for one chat. For a person, on a channel holding the `lid_lookup` grant, both of their addresses (phone JID and LID) are read and merged into one timeline; `merge` says whether that happened and, if not, why. In a group, each sender is presented as one identity: `sender_jid` is their phone JID where known, `sender_lid` the LID they were stored under. Each message says which chat it is filed under (`source_chat`). Page with `before`: pass the previous page's `next_before` until it is absent. Every page returned is recorded in this channel's API access records (who read it, which chats, how many messages; never the content).

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Continue from a previous page: its `next_before`, exactly as returned. Any other value is a 400.

chats.description: The chat addresses this page was read from.

merge.description: `merged`: both of the person's addresses were read. `none_known`: no other address is known for them. `not_granted`: this channel does not hold the `lid_lookup` grant, so only the named address was read. `not_a_person`: a group (one chat).

next_before.description: Present when older messages exist: pass it as `before` for the next page.

post.summary: Check to ensure phone numbers are still on WhatsApp
post.description: Asks WhatsApp about up to 50 numbers in one call (the default; an operator can configure it) and answers at once. For a long list use `createNumberCheck`, which runs in the background. This raw call does not use the cache. On a customer channel it draws on the same daily and hourly check allowance as a background check, and checks are spaced out: a call inside the gap returns 429 `checks_spaced_out`, and a call the allowance cannot cover returns 429 `check_allowance_used`, each at once with `retry_after`. The number checker is included with every paid number. The account needs at least one active non-sandbox channel, whether covered by payment or a complimentary, promotional or admin grant. Without one, this route returns 403 `number_checker_requires_paid_number`. Checks run only on non-sandbox channels; a sandbox request from an eligible account returns 403 `number_checker_requires_non_sandbox_channel`. `is_business` appears only when `true`: omitted means not known to be a verified business, never "personal". A check is a point-in-time answer from WhatsApp and can be wrong or out of date by the time you use it. It is not a promise that a message will be delivered.

403.description: The account has no active non-sandbox channel (`number_checker_requires_paid_number`), or the requested channel is sandbox (`number_checker_requires_non_sandbox_channel`).

get.description: Read the contact identified by who through the named channel. Returns the contact details known to that channel.

put.description: Save or update a contact identified by who for the named channel using the supplied contact fields.

delete.description: Clears the contact's stored names and, where phone writes are enabled, removes the contact from the linked phone's contact list through the same queue as a save. Idempotent: removing a contact that is not stored, or already removed, answers 200. handset is removed once the phone's app state confirmed the removal. Without phone writes enabled it answers off and only the stored names are cleared. While the channel's phone writes are halted it behaves exactly as a save: the names are cleared, nothing is sent to the phone, and handset is failed. A removal that was queued waits until an operator clears the halt; one that could not be queued is not made, so send it again once the halt is cleared.

post.summary: Start a number check to ensure a list of numbers are still on WhatsApp
post.description: Creates a check that runs in the background on this channel's own number and returns at once (201). Checks run in the background and are spaced out, and each number has a daily check allowance, so a long list can take hours or days; it keeps running if you close the app. Poll `getNumberCheck` for progress, and read the rows with `getNumberCheckResults` at any time, partial results included. The channel must be connected now. Up to 10000 numbers per check; a row that is not a phone number is kept and marked `invalid` with the reason, never dropped. A repeat of a number checked recently is answered from the cache (7 days for a number that is on WhatsApp, 24 hours for one that is not) without asking WhatsApp or using the allowance; `refresh: true` asks again. There is no setting to make a check faster. The number checker is included with every paid number. The account needs at least one active non-sandbox channel, whether covered by payment or a complimentary, promotional or admin grant. Without one, this route returns 403 `number_checker_requires_paid_number`. Checks run only on non-sandbox channels; a sandbox request from an eligible account returns 403 `number_checker_requires_non_sandbox_channel`. A check is a point-in-time answer from WhatsApp and can be wrong or out of date by the time you use it. It is not a promise that a message will be delivered.

numbers.description: The numbers, as you have them. A leading `+`, spaces, dashes and brackets are fine; start with the country code.

refresh.description: Ask WhatsApp again even for numbers answered within the cache window. Default false.

403.description: The account has no active non-sandbox channel (`number_checker_requires_paid_number`), or the requested channel is sandbox (`number_checker_requires_non_sandbox_channel`).

get.summary: Read a number check: progress, allowance, estimate and pause reason
get.description: `state` is `queued`, `running`, `paused`, `done`, `canceled` or `failed`. A `paused` check says why in `pause`, and when it resumes by itself in `pause.resume_at`; a pause for the daily or hourly allowance, or for a slow-down, is not an error and loses nothing. For `channel_down`, reconnect the channel and call `resumeNumberCheck`. An account suspension must be resolved before checks can continue. `budget` shows what is left today and this hour, and `eta` is an estimate of when the check finishes. A failed check reports its terminal code and reason in `failure`; an upstream failure uses `check_failed`. It does not mean a number is unregistered. Another channel's check answers `not_found`.

403.description: The account has no active non-sandbox channel (`number_checker_requires_paid_number`), or the requested channel is sandbox (`number_checker_requires_non_sandbox_channel`).

get.summary: Read a number check's rows, partial results included
get.description: Rows come back in the order you gave them, with `status` `pending` for the ones not yet checked. Page with `offset` and `limit`; filter with `status`. `is_business` appears only when `true`: omitted means not known to be a verified business, never "personal". `lid` is WhatsApp's alternate ID for the number, when WhatsApp gave one. A check is a point-in-time answer from WhatsApp and can be wrong or out of date by the time you use it. It is not a promise that a message will be delivered. The console's Number checker page exports the same rows as a CSV file.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only rows with these statuses, comma-separated: `pending`, `registered`, `not_registered`, `invalid`, `error`.

total.description: Rows matching the filter, across all pages.

post.description: The rows checked so far stay readable. Cancelling a check that already finished changes nothing.

403.description: The account has no active non-sandbox channel (`number_checker_requires_paid_number`), or the requested channel is sandbox (`number_checker_requires_non_sandbox_channel`).

post.summary: Resume a check paused because the channel was not connected
post.description: Honoured only for a pause with code `channel_down`, once the channel is connected again and its status is not Bad. Every other pause ends by itself at `pause.resume_at`; resuming one answers 400.

post.description: JPEG or PNG, at most 5 MiB. The media is fetched by the gateway from `url`. The URL must be http or https, carry no credentials, and resolve to a public internet address; it may redirect at most 3 times, and every hop is held to the same rule. It must answer 2xx within 30 seconds. The message type WhatsApp is told comes from the bytes, not from the URL's Content-Type. A media message counts as one message against the daily message allowance (sandbox channels), the same as a text, whatever its size. Errors: `media_type_unsupported` and `media_fetch_failed` (400) are about the media; `media_too_large` is 400 when the media is fetched from a URL and 413 when the uploaded file (multipart) is over the limit; `media_upload_failed` (502) means the upload to WhatsApp failed and nothing was sent, so retrying is safe. A media send can also answer 429 `gateway_busy` with `bound: "media"` when the gateway is holding as many media payloads as it can; retry after the Retry-After header (10 seconds).

delete.description: Deletes for everyone, in a chat or a group, a message this channel's number sent (through the API or on the paired phone) and this channel has in its message log. Only your own messages: someone else's answers 403 `not_own_message` (deleting others' messages as a group admin is not offered). A message more than 48 hours old answers 409 `revoke_window_passed`, and one not in the log 404 `message_not_found`; neither sends anything. IDEMPOTENT: deleting a message the log already records as deleted answers 200 with `status: "already_revoked"` and sends nothing; a delete of the same message while one is still running answers 409 `revoke_in_progress`. A delete counts as one message against the daily message allowance (sandbox channels), as a reaction does. The log keeps the message and marks it with `revoked_at`. A delete made on the paired phone, or by the sender of a message you received, arrives as a `message` webhook event of type `protocol` carrying `revoke.message_id`.

put.description: Reacts with one emoji to a message in this channel's log; a new reaction replaces this channel's earlier one. Counts as one message against the daily message allowance (sandbox channels). A message this channel has no record of answers 404 `message_not_found`.

delete.description: Removes this channel's reaction to a message. Counts as one message against the daily message allowance (sandbox channels), as WhatsApp sends it as one.

post.description: Send read receipts for the supplied message identifiers in the specified chat through the named channel.

up_to.description: Only with message_ids. When true, every unread message in the chat at or before the newest id you pass is also marked read, each to its own sender in a group, so everyone you have read up to sees it. receipted then counts those messages too; an id you pass that is already read is not marked again. Without it (the default) only the ids you pass are marked. When the unread range holds more than 5 senders or 500 messages, only the oldest unread messages are marked (at most 5 senders and 500 messages per request), the answer carries partial: true, and the rest stays unread: send the same request again to continue. partial is absent when everything was marked. A request that fails after a receipt went out is never a 4xx: it is 502 receipt_partial with receipted, the count already marked.

partial.description: Present only when up_to marked just the oldest part of a range past 5 senders or 500 messages. The rest is still unread; send the same request again to continue.

get.description: Warming is available only to accounts the gateway has enabled it for. For any other channel this route answers `not_found`.

put.summary: Turn warming on or off for this channel
put.description:
The first switch-on of an account must carry acknowledge, which records the account's acceptance of this text (version 2026-10-13):

> Warming sends short, pre-written chat messages between your own channels, automatically, from your numbers. You do not write these messages. HelloHop does, and sends them on your behalf. They are ordinary WhatsApp messages from your numbers: you will see the chats on your phones, and they count toward your sandbox allowances.
>
> WhatsApp decides what it allows. Warming is meant to lower the risk of a restriction, but WhatsApp can still restrict or ban any number, including one that is warming, for reasons we cannot see and cannot reverse. A restriction or ban alone does not entitle you to a refund or compensation. Refund rights required by law and the liability exceptions in Terms section 13 still apply.
>
> You can turn warming off for any number at any time. It stops before the next message.
>
> I understand that HelloHop will send pre-written messages from my numbers on my behalf, and that WhatsApp may still restrict or ban a number that is warming. I own these numbers or am authorized to operate them, and I accept that risk.

Turning it on needs the account owner's acknowledgement of the warming terms: either recorded earlier (`warming_ack_required` until it is) or sent here as `acknowledge`. After a safety stop the number cools down first (`warming_cooldown`, with `restart_after`); a restart after that stop also needs `restart_ack: true` (`warming_restart_ack_required`). Only `enabled`, `restart_ack` and `acknowledge` are accepted; any other field is refused. A successful call returns the channel (`Session`); its `warming` field holds the same object `GET` returns. Available only to accounts the gateway has enabled warming for; otherwise `not_found`.

restart_ack.description: Confirms a restart after a safety stop.

text_version.description: The version of the warming terms being acknowledged. Checked only while the account has not yet acknowledged the current version: then an unknown version is `warming_ack_version_unknown`. Once the account has acknowledged the current version, a supplied value is ignored and enabling can succeed.

put.summary: Choose whether this channel's receivers get warming traffic
put.description: Off by default. When on, this channel's webhook receivers also receive the events its warming traffic produces, marked `warming: true`. Available only to accounts the gateway has enabled warming for; otherwise `not_found`.

BadRequest.description: The request was refused as sent.

PayloadTooLarge.description: An uploaded file (multipart/form-data) is larger than its media type allows (media_too_large).

Unauthorized.description: Missing, invalid or stale token, or a channel this token does not open.

Forbidden.description: The token is valid and may not do this.

NotFound.description: The route or the named object does not exist.

Conflict.description: The channel's state does not allow this, for example not_linked or stood_down.

TooManyRequests.description: A gateway flood guard or the webhook-test cooldown (rate_limited, with a Retry-After header), the gateway being busy with this channel's earlier requests (gateway_busy, Retry-After: 1), a sandbox channel's allowance (sandbox_allowance_exceeded, with Retry-After), an operator stop (daily_send_cap_exceeded), a raw number check inside the channel's gap (checks_spaced_out, with Retry-After) or past its check allowance (check_allowance_used, with Retry-After and resets_at), an optional warm-up protection allowance (daily_cap_<class>, only when warm-up protection is on), a history request inside its rate limit (history_request_too_soon, with Retry-After), or WhatsApp throttling the number (whatsapp_rate_limited, no Retry-After). Paid numbers have no gateway allowance. `code` says which: the bodies never share one.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait. Sent with rate_limited, gateway_busy, sandbox_allowance_exceeded, checks_spaced_out and check_allowance_used.

InternalError.description: The gateway could not complete the request.

BadGateway.description: The service behind the gateway could not be reached or answered unusably. Retry.

Unavailable.description: Temporarily unavailable, for example the token could not be checked, the gateway could not confirm its own account setup (operator_unresolved, with a Retry-After header), or a call made under a phone lane reached the lane's deadline (lane_reclaimed, with a Retry-After header and `ambiguous`). Unless the error explicitly says nothing was sent (for example `ambiguous: false`), treat any write as possibly applied; list or read the state of what you changed before retrying a write; never re-create (e.g. a group) without reading/listing first; reads can be retried after a short back-off. Honor Retry-After when present.

ReadBadGateway.description: Either the service behind the gateway could not be reached (retry), or, with code `receipt_partial`, some read receipts went out before the request failed: `receipted` is how many messages were marked. Do not resend a `receipt_partial` request as is.

SendUnconfirmed.description: The outcome is unknown. Look up `id` in history before resending.

ErrorCode.description: Stable machine-readable error code. Branch on this, not on `error`. A client should treat an unknown code as a generic failure.

error.description: Human-readable message. It can change; do not parse it.

reason.description: Present when the request failed on a connection-level error (a connect, a relink, a proxy change that reconnects, or any call whose socket or proxy failed). `error` is then a fixed sentence for this reason. For a channel or customer caller `error` is always a fixed sentence for its `code`, or the gateway's own validation message; the underlying error text is never returned.

window.description: The ceiling that refused the request, for example token.send. Not a closed list.

WhatsAppRateLimitError.description: WhatsApp itself throttled the linked number (an IQ 429), not a ceiling of ours. No Retry-After is sent: WhatsApp does not say how long. Back off and retry later.

OperatorUnresolvedError.description: The gateway could not confirm its own account setup for a moment, so it could not decide whether this channel may send. Nothing about the channel is wrong. Retry after the Retry-After header (5 seconds).

LaneReclaimedError.description: A call made under a phone lane reached the lane's deadline. Retry after the Retry-After header (1 second). `ambiguous` is always present: false means the call was refused before it was sent, so nothing reached WhatsApp and a plain retry is safe; true means the call was sent and its outcome is unknown, so a group add may already have applied: retry at your normal pace and treat "already a participant" as success.

ambiguous.description: false: refused before it was sent, nothing reached WhatsApp. true: sent, outcome unknown.

WarmingCooldownError.description: This number was stopped for safety and is cooling down. `restart_after` is when warming may be turned on again, or null when there is no recorded end and the gateway operator clears it.

HistoryRequestTooSoonError.description: A history request inside its rate limit: one per channel every 30 seconds, one per chat every 5 minutes. Retry after the Retry-After header.

GatewayBusyError.description: The gateway has too many requests in flight to take this one, or is holding as many media sends as it can. `bound` names the limit that refused it: this channel's own in-flight requests, all of this account's channels together, the gateway's shared pool, or `media` for media sends. Never queued: retry after the Retry-After header (1 second, or 10 seconds for `media`).

bound.description: Which limit refused the request. May be absent.

CheckAllowanceError.description: A raw number check on a customer channel arrived inside the channel's gap (`checks_spaced_out`) or past its daily or hourly check allowance (`check_allowance_used`). Never queued: retry after the Retry-After header. An allowance refusal also carries `window`, `cap`, `used` and `resets_at`.

SandboxAllowanceError.description: A sandbox channel reached one of its allowances (180 messages a day, 10 new chats a month, 5 group adds a day, 1,500 API calls a month; days and months in Bangkok time, UTC+7). Every request made with the sandbox channel's key counts as an API call, reads included. Sent with a Retry-After header. Paid channels never receive it.

DailySendCapError.description: An operator stop: the operator has stopped sends on this channel (a ceiling of 0), or the channel is in the operator's warming programme. Paid numbers have no daily message allowance, so on a customer channel this means the operator acted.

receipted.description: How many messages were marked read before the request failed. Do not resend the same request.

id.description: The logged row of this send. Look it up in history before resending.

status.description: WhatsApp's servers accepted the message. Not a delivery receipt.

id.description: The delete's own message id. Absent when `status` is `already_revoked`.

timestamp.description: WhatsApp's time on the delete. Absent when `status` is `already_revoked`.

status.description: `server_ack`: the delete was sent and WhatsApp's servers accepted it. `already_revoked`: the log already records this message as deleted; nothing was sent and nothing counted.

is_incognito.description: Absent on this API: it is filled only by a hydrate read, and the public API relays no query string.

jid.description: The address as you sent it.

status.description: `ok`, `error_<status>`, or `unknown` when the change may have applied; read the group before retrying.

lid.description: The number's LID (alternate WhatsApp ID) from the same answer. Omitted when WhatsApp gave none.

phone_e164.description: The number actually checked, normalized to international form with a leading +.

country.description: Two-letter country of the number, when known.

cached.description: `true` when the answer came from the number checker's cache. The raw check never does.

age_seconds.description: How old a cached answer is.

error.description: Set when WhatsApp gave no answer for this number (for example `no_answer`). This is not the same as `registered: false`.

ContactCheck.description: One number's answer. `is_business` appears only when `true` and means WhatsApp's answer carried a verified business name: omitted means not known to be a verified business, never "personal". The raw check does not use the cache; a long list can run as a background number check. A check is a point-in-time answer from WhatsApp and can be wrong or out of date by the time you use it. It is not a promise that a message will be delivered.

handset.description: Whether the linked phone holds this contact under the names above. saved: the phone confirmed these names (including when it already held them). pending: the write to the phone is queued. unknown: a write may or may not have reached the phone. failed: the write was not made by this request: no phone number is known for this contact yet or the queue is full (it will not be made), or the channel's phone writes are halted (a write that was queued waits and is made once an operator clears the halt; one that could not be queued is not made, so send it again once the halt is cleared). off: phone writes are not enabled on this channel, so the contact is saved here only (or, after a remove, removed here only). removed: the phone confirmed the contact is not in its contact list (after a remove, or deleted on the phone).

reason.description: Plain-language reason, safe to show as is.

resume_at.description: When the check resumes by itself. Absent when it waits for the channel to reconnect.

NumberCheckBudget.description: The check allowance for a channel: what is left today and this hour. There is one figure, the lowest that applies.

tier.description: Allowance tier by number age, for example `Week 1` or `Mature`.

age_known.description: False when the number's age is not known; it is then treated as the newest tier.

daily_budget.description: Live lookups allowed per day (Bangkok day).

source.description: Which allowance applies: the checker's own, or the channel's warm-up allowance.

NumberCheckFailure.description: The terminal reason for a failed number check.

reason.description: Plain-language reason, safe to show as is.

done.description: Rows no longer pending, invalid rows included.

invalid.description: Rows that are not phone numbers; each is kept with its reason.

live_lookups.description: Numbers asked of WhatsApp so far.

refresh.description: Present and true when the check was created with `refresh`.

eta.description: Estimated finish. Absent while the channel is down.

finished_at.description: Absent until the check is done, canceled or failed.

NumberCheckResult.description: One row of a number check. A check is a point-in-time answer from WhatsApp and can be wrong or out of date by the time you use it. It is not a promise that a message will be delivered.

input.description: The row as you gave it.

phone_e164.description: The number checked, normalized to international form with a leading +. Absent on an invalid row.

status.description: `pending` not yet checked, `registered` on WhatsApp, `not_registered` not on WhatsApp, `invalid` not a phone number (see `error`), `error` WhatsApp gave no answer (never cached, not the same as not registered).

jid.description: The WhatsApp address, when on WhatsApp.

lid.description: The LID from the same answer, when WhatsApp gave one.

is_business.description: Appears only when `true`: WhatsApp's answer carried a verified business name. Omitted means not known to be a verified business, never personal.

verified_name.description: The verified business name, when there is one.

cached.description: True when answered from the cache.

age_seconds.description: How old a cached answer is.

error.description: Why a row is `invalid`, or what went wrong for an `error` row.

pn.description: Phone-number address (user JID). Absent when no phone number is known for the LID.

lid.description: The LID address. Absent when no LID is known for the phone number.

LIDMapping.description: One entry of the gateway's LID map. Both keys are omitted when empty, so an unknown mapping is a 200 with the looked-up key only.

reason_code.description: Why warming is in this state.

stale.description: True when the progress figures could not be read fresh, so they are the last known rather than current.

webhook_include_warming.description: Whether this channel's webhook receivers get warming traffic (see PUT warming/webhooks).

unlinked.description: true while this channel has held a number and an unlink released it. Link the same channel again; do not create a new one.

plan.description: sandbox: the account's free sandbox channel, which has daily allowances (SandboxAllowanceError). paid: no gateway allowances. comp: a channel covered by the account's channel grant rather than a subscription. internal: a channel owned by the gateway operator's own account.

comp_granted.description: true for a comp channel the account's channel grant covers now. Absent otherwise.

last_error.description: Why the last connection attempt or state change failed, as one of a fixed set of sentences. It never quotes the underlying error.

connected_stale.description: True when `connected` could not be observed by this read, so it is the last known state rather than a fresh one. Absent when the read is fresh.

warming.description: The channel's warming state. A channel token or a customer account receives the customer shape (`CustomerWarming`), present only when customer warming is on for the account and the channel is admitted, and it is the `warming` of the `PUT /sessions/{name}/warming` response. The operator receives the enrollment form below.

number_checker_eligible.description: Whether this non-sandbox channel is active and the owning account has at least one active non-sandbox channel. Included with every paid number; complimentary, promotional and admin grants qualify. A disconnected channel can be eligible, but must connect before starting a check.

Session.description: The channel's state. This is every field the public API returns for a session. The fields listed under x-operator-only (the operator's phone lane and the legacy send_cap_exempt row kept for rollback) are operator-only: they are never returned to a channel token or to a customer account, only to the operator.

level.description: too_early is neutral in the overall: good plus too_early reads good when at least one reading is measured good; all too_early reads watch ('Not enough data yet'); a reading that could not be measured reads watch.

measured_at.description: Time this reading was computed. A replayed reading keeps its original compute time.

evidence_at.description: Time the underlying evidence was measured, or null when there is no recorded measurement.

live.description: Whether this reading uses live state rather than a recorded measurement.

data.description: Reading-specific fields; other keys may appear. A computed `lifetime` carries `source`, `days`, `is_lower_bound` and `linked_at`; `stood_down` carries `refused` and the fields below.

source.description: `lifetime` only: where the age was measured from.

days.description: `lifetime` only: whole days from `linked_at` to `measured_at`, floored. A lower bound when `is_lower_bound` is true.

is_lower_bound.description: `lifetime` only: true when the age comes from the earliest message, so the real age is at least this.

linked_at.description: `lifetime` only: the instant the age is measured from. A `registration_date` source is a calendar date encoded as UTC midnight.

refused.description: `stood_down` only: the policy-only refusal the warmer reads, independent of `level`.

blocked.description: `stood_down` only: the identity guard is blocking the channel.

refusal_kind.description: `stood_down` only: why a send would be refused, empty when none.

cap_source.description: `stood_down` only: where the daily ceiling comes from (`none` when no ceiling applies).

since.description: `stood_down` only: when the unlink was recorded.

restricted_at.description: `stood_down` only: present for a severe WhatsApp logout.

unreadable.description: Present and true when the reading could not be taken.

level.description: Always exactly good, watch or bad, never none or too_early (changed 2026-10-20). Bad if any reading is bad; else watch if any reading is watch or could not be measured, or the report is waiting or stale; else good. too_early is neutral: good plus too_early reads good when at least one reading is measured good; all too_early reads watch ('Not enough data yet'); a reading that could not be measured reads watch.

measured_at.description: Time this reading was computed. A replayed reading keeps its original compute time.

evidence_at.description: Time the underlying evidence was measured, or null when there is no recorded measurement.

live.description: Whether this reading uses live state rather than a recorded measurement.

data.description: Reading-specific fields; other keys may appear. A computed `lifetime` carries `source`, `days`, `is_lower_bound` and `linked_at`; `stood_down` carries `refused` and the fields below.

source.description: `lifetime` only: where the age was measured from.

days.description: `lifetime` only: whole days from `linked_at` to `measured_at`, floored. A lower bound when `is_lower_bound` is true.

is_lower_bound.description: `lifetime` only: true when the age comes from the earliest message, so the real age is at least this.

linked_at.description: `lifetime` only: the instant the age is measured from. A `registration_date` source is a calendar date encoded as UTC midnight.

refused.description: `stood_down` only: the policy-only refusal the warmer reads, independent of `level`.

blocked.description: `stood_down` only: the identity guard is blocking the channel.

refusal_kind.description: `stood_down` only: why a send would be refused, empty when none.

cap_source.description: `stood_down` only: where the daily ceiling comes from (`none` when no ceiling applies).

since.description: `stood_down` only: when the unlink was recorded.

restricted_at.description: `stood_down` only: present for a severe WhatsApp logout.

unreadable.description: Present and true when the reading could not be taken.

overall.description: Changed 2026-10-20: overall.level is always good, watch or bad and no longer returns none. A waiting or stale report reads watch (or bad when a measured reading is bad).

type.description: The kind of message. Values include text, image, video, document, audio, sticker, contact, contact_list, location, live_location, poll, poll_vote, reaction, protocol, short (a video note), group_invite and unknown (a message that cannot be described). New values can be added, so handle a value you do not recognize the way you handle unknown.

poll.description: A poll's structure (type `poll`), or a vote's (type `poll_vote`).

multiple.description: type `poll`: more than one option may be chosen.

selected.description: type `poll_vote`: the chosen options, by name. A readable vote with no `selected` and no `unresolved` is an un-vote: the voter withdrew their choice.

unresolved.description: type `poll_vote`: chosen options that could not be named (the poll is not in this channel's log).

unreadable.description: type `poll_vote`: the vote could not be decrypted; `selected` means nothing.

revoked_at.description: When this message was deleted for everyone (by this number or by its sender). Absent if it was not. The log keeps the message's content.

sender_pn_resolved.description: Present, and false, only when the sender was stored under a LID whose phone number is not known; `sender_jid` then holds the LID.

quoted_author_lid.description: The LID the quoted message's author was named by, when it was; `quoted_author` is then their phone JID where known.

source.description: Conversation reads: `live` for a message captured while the channel was connected, `history_sync` for one the paired phone sent as history (stored because `store_history_sync` is on).

source_chat.description: Conversation reads: the chat address this message is filed under in the log (a person's phone JID or LID, or the group).

reaction.description: type `reaction`: the message reacted to. `text` is the emoji; `removed` marks a removal. Absent on reactions logged before 2026-10-05.

revoke.description: A delete for everyone (type `revoke`, sent by this number; type `protocol`, observed): the message it names. Whether the delete took effect is that message's `revoked_at`. Absent on deletes logged before 2026-10-05.

events.description: Event types to receive. Omit for every type.

secret.description: Signs this receiver's deliveries. Required for a new receiver. On a receiver you already saved, omit it (or send an empty string) to keep the stored secret; send a new value of at least 24 characters to replace it. A secret cannot be removed: delete the receiver and add it again with a new one.
